wiki_text: In November 2025, the International Finance Corporation (IFC, the World Bank's private-sector investment arm) signed an advisory agreement with the Government of Lebanon, acting as lead transaction advisor -- working alongside Lebanon's High Council for Privatization and PPPs and the Ministry of Energy and Water -- to structure a gas-to-power public-private partnership at Deir Ammar. The project comprises three components: (1) the FSRU itself, to import, store, and regasify LNG; (2) modernization of the existing 465 MW Deir Ammar I plant into a higher-capacity independent power producer; and (3) construction of a new 825 MW combined-cycle gas turbine plant, Deir Ammar II. This followed World Bank Expression-of-Interest tenders opened in June 2025 for legal, environmental/social, and technical transaction advisors on the same project. Separately, in January 2026 Egypt and Lebanon signed an MoU to supply pipeline gas to the Deir Ammar Power Plant via Egypt's Idku/Damietta LNG infrastructure and the Arab Gas Pipeline -- a parallel, non-marine gas-supply track distinct from the FSRU's ship-borne LNG import, pending completion of the FSRU itself.
